panels.title: Safety first: are urgent complaints getting human attention?

options.content: Use a fictional harm complaint, review its model and effective severity, then run the **quality** replay in the app. A safety flag is not necessarily a model miss. Replay recall is based on examples, not live model accuracy. [Complaint Operations](/d/complaint-operations) | [Drift and Incident](/d/drift-incident) | [Jaeger](http://localhost:16686)

panels.description: Cases with a covered safety signal, including cases already predicted as SEV1. This is not a count of confirmed model misses.
panels.title: Cases with a safety flag

panels.description: Authorized reviews that created a simulated queue entry, grouped by live model or scripted test mode.
panels.title: Human-approved simulated routes

panels.description: Average recall recorded by repeated deterministic quality replays. Scripted fixture uses fixture responses; controlled scenario uses label-derived examples. Before safeguards uses the initial severity; after safeguards includes replay safeguards. Not measured live accuracy.

targets.expr: sum by (pack, metric_type) (evaluation_sev1_recall_sum{replay="quality"}) / sum by (pack, metric_type) (evaluation_sev1_recall_count{replay="quality"})

panels.title: SEV1 recall - quality replay

panels.description: Count of successfully classified complaints by effective severity after safeguards, including cases where drafting later failed. SEV1 is the most urgent. Lines rise as classifications are saved; the legend shows the latest counter value. Counters start when this instrumentation is deployed and can reset on restart. A severity appears after it is observed; this is not measured model accuracy.
panels.title: Complaint severity - count and trend
